system_prompt:
You are a working research mathematician in computational
complexity theory, with deep knowledge across pure mathematics. Your task: propose
ONE genuinely novel conjecture linking a branch of mathematics RARELY applied to
complexity theory with a specific complexity-theoretic object (SAT, resolution
proofs, boolean circuits, communication complexity, etc).

Hard requirements:
  1. NEVER repeat or trivially rephrase an item in the blacklist below.
  2. The linkage (field_A × field_B) must be one you believe has <5 papers.
  3. The conjecture must be TESTABLE on instances of size n ≤ 40 in < 240 seconds
     of pure Python (no external solvers allowed; small DPLL is fine). Use
     30 random seeds for statistical robustness.
  4. Stated as a concrete quantitative relation (e.g., "E[X(instance)] = Θ(f(n))"
     or "for all instances with property P, property Q holds"), not vague.
  5. Give a falsifier-friendly formulation (one counterexample refutes it).
  6. MUST include a CONSTRUCTIVE MAPPING: a concrete, coded-in-50-lines-of-python
     procedure that transforms the instance into the field_A object. If the
     invariant requires advanced algebraic machinery (Coxeter groups, étale
     cohomology, motives, Langlands dual, etc.) without a computational shortcut,
     REJECT this idea and pick another. Example of GOOD: "compute the
     Grothendieck-Witt class of the clause-indicator polynomial modulo 2" —
     concrete. Example of BAD: "associate a motive to each CNF" — uncomputable.

Output STRICT JSON (no markdown, no preamble), with keys:
  title         — short, specific (≤ 70 chars)
  field_A       — the mathematical branch (e.g. "Arakelov geometry", "free probability")
  field_B       — the complexity object (e.g. "DPLL search tree", "Frege proof depth")
  statement     — precise mathematical statement, ≤ 3 sentences
  rationale     — why this bridge might expose structure, ≤ 3 sentences
  test_strategy — concrete plan: what to generate, what to measure, what the
                  correlation/bound to check is. ≤ 4 sentences.

Do not use any field that already appears in the blacklist. Avoid:
information theory on resolution (SEC-MI, done), Ollivier-Ricci on SAT graphs
(Skenderi 2025), tropical rank of ±1 matrices (trivial).

  title: Slice Rank of Layer-Variable Tensor Lower-Bounds Read-Twice BP Size for IP_2
  statement: For a read-k branching program P with vertex set V(P), define the layer-variable tensor T_P ∈ F_2^{|V|×|V|×n} by T_P[u,v,j] := (number of edges u→v labelled by a literal of x_j) mod 2, and let ρ(P) := slice_rank_{F_2}(T_P). Conjecture (B) For every (unrestricted) branching program P that computes IP_2 on n variables, ρ(P) ≥ n/8; in particular any read-twice P for IP_2 satisfies |V(P)| ≥ 2^{n/48}, and a single (P,ρ) pair refuting either inequality falsifies the claim.
  rationale: Slice rank is the F_2 invariant that drove the cap-set collapse: it measures how far a 3-tensor is from being decomposable along axis-aligned slabs, and read-twice forces the variable axis of T_P to be a sparse, low-multiplicity fiber pattern — exactly the regime where Tao-style slice arguments give logarithmic bounds. Conversely, IP_2 is the canonical bilinear obstruction, and any BP encoding it must spread the x_j-fibers of T_P across many slices because each x_j actually multiplies a distinct y_j, conjecturally producing a partition-rank-style anti-cap configuration with linear slice rank. The bridge is novel because slice rank has been deployed for cap sets, sunflower bounds, and matrix multiplication exponent, but never (to <5 papers) as a BP-size lower-bound invariant.
  test_strategy: For each n ∈ {6,8,10,12,14,16,18,20} and 30 random seeds, generate a random read-twice BP P (width w∈{2,3,4}, layered, each variable reused exactly twice) and compute T_P; obtain a slice-rank upper bound by greedy peeling (at each step, find the axis i ∈ {1,2,3} and rank-1 vector v whose outer slice maximally reduces remaining F_2 support, subtract, recurse) and confirm ρ(P) ≤ 6·⌈log_2 |V|⌉ on every sample. For Conjecture B, build the canonical layered IP_2 BP for n ∈ {4,6,8,10,12} (states track running parity of x_i·y_i prefixes) and lower-bound ρ via the partition-rank dual: maximise over balanced 2-colourings of the j-axis the F_2 rank of the induced V²×(n/2) flattening minus the rank absorbed into a single u- or v-slice, certifying ≥ n/8. Pre-registered support condition: ≥27/30 read-twice samples satisfy ρ ≤ 6 log_2|V| AND every IP_2 BP achieves ρ ≥ n/8; any single counterexample of either inequality falsifies. Total runtime ≤240s in pure Python using bitset F_2 arithmetic.
  acceptance_criterion: Across 30 seeds for each n∈{6,8,10,12,14,16,18,20} (read-twice BPs, w∈{2,3,4}), greedy slice-rank upper bound ρ(P) must satisfy ρ ≤ 6·⌈log_2|V(P)|⌉ on ≥27/30 seeds per n; and for canonical IP_2 BPs at n∈{4,6,8,10,12}, partition-rank lower bound must give ρ ≥ ⌈n/8⌉ for every n.
